notes: Passage-level batch from Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam Canto 4, chapters 1, 8, 10, 13–15, 24, 30–31, using Vedabase verse text and English translation. All claims point to the verse translation; no purport is used.

The batch includes named genealogies from Manu, Dakṣa, Aṅgirā, Pulastya, Pulaha, Vasiṣṭha, Bhṛgu, Dhruva, Vena/Pṛthu, and the Pracetās. Named sons/daughters are included only where the verse gives their names. Anonymous groups are not turned into individuals.

The Dakṣa reborn from Māriṣā is attached to the existing Dakṣa node because 4.30.49 explicitly calls him the same Prajāpati; no duplicate rebirth node is retained. The ten Pracetās are represented once as an explicitly named collective because the cited passages do not give their personal names; this is not counted as an individually named person. No claims infer which brother fathered Māriṣā’s child.

Reused clear graph IDs: Dakṣa, Śiva, Indra, Agni, Soma, Varuṇa, Sūrya, Vasiṣṭha, Atri, Arundhatī, Brahmā, Viṣṇu/Yajña, Vāyu, Dharma, Kubera, Yama, Rāvaṇa, Vibhīṣaṇa, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Bhṛgu, Marīci and Māriṣā. Dhruva and Pṛthu are source-scoped to avoid merging with similarly named graph figures without a reviewed cross-witness identity check.

Explicit within-batch title/name equivalences represented once include Vijitāśva/Antardhāna, Barhiṣat/Prācīnabarhi, and Uśanā/Kavi. The two Puṣkariṇīs and the Aṅgirā’s wife Śraddhā versus Dakṣa’s daughter Śraddhā remain distinct.

Some entries are personified virtues named as Dakṣa’s daughters and Dharma’s children, and 4.8.2–4 personifications in Adharma’s genealogy. They are treated as individual named figures because the verse translation directly assigns them kinship relations; no purport-only allegory is used.

The translation identifies Agastya as becoming Dahrāgni in his next birth; that relation is recorded as a source claim rather than a generic alias. Māriṣā reuses the existing Viṣṇu Purāṇa Canto 4 anchor because the named person and Pracetās genealogy match, but all claims remain linked to Bhāgavata verses.
